slides.say: A, B and C represent digits, and A is bigger than C, which is bigger than zero. Which of the following could be the value of A B C minus C B A?
A three-digit number minus its reversal. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, with the algebraic form, and then plugging in numbers.

[short pause] Let's start with the algebraic form. A B C is a hundred A, plus ten B, plus C. C B A is a hundred C, plus ten B, plus A. Subtract, and the middle digit cancels. Ninety-nine A minus ninety-nine C.
at: A B C is a hundred A

slides.say: That's ninety-nine times, in brackets, A minus C. So the answer must be a multiple of ninety-nine.

Three-digit multiples of ninety-nine have nine in the middle, and the outer digits add up to nine. One ninety-eight, two ninety-seven, three ninety-six. Four fifty-nine has five in the middle, out. Four eighty-four, eight, out. Five forty, four, out.
Four ninety-five has nine in the middle, and four plus five is nine. It's ninety-nine times five. Choice number three is our answer.
at: Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Another way, plugging in numbers. What's different? We don't write any algebra, we let a few examples show the pattern. Three twelve minus two thirteen is ninety-nine. Five twenty-three minus three twenty-five is one ninety-eight. Always multiples of ninety-nine.
And four ninety-five can really happen. With A minus C five, six twenty-one minus one twenty-six is four ninety-five. Choice number three. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: is four ninety-five. Choice number three
